answer: Dock every agent's influence at the harbor registry: each identity posts a bond and gets one non-transferable jade stamp. Each settlement draws a co-signing quorum from the opal beacon, passing only when a full quorum of distinct jade stamps signs. An attacker wanting N fake votes must buy N jade stamps at full bond price. But opal draws are public, so sybil quorums overlap: when one mis-signs, every jade stamp in it burns, and N clones in overlapping quorums lose roughly N² bonds while an honest agent risks one stamp. Quorum math, not delays or fees, makes cloning superlinearly expensive.
